independentFinding: I viewed the image before reading any reviewer notes, and on first pass at full-frame scale I misread the pale object as a cracked stone lid, so I magnified it twice. Magnified, it is a single thin, roughly square sheet of parchment lying flat on the dark stone slab, and it is TORN. Both halves lie coplanar with the slab top — there is no tented V, no valley, no pages rising away from a centre line. The dark line between them is ragged and irregular in width, with uneven fibrous edges and the two sides slightly offset: a tear, not a straight bound gutter. The tear runs all the way through the sheet's near edge, notching it into two separately drooping corners — an open book lying spine-toward-the-viewer would show a continuous bound edge there, not a gap. The near edge is a single thin lip that curls down over the slab's chamfered corner; there is no stacked page-block. The sword's bright point rests exactly at the head of the tear. Elsewhere: one crowned, dark-robed figure facing the viewer, face lost in shadow under a tall spiked crown, one hand on the sword, the other gripping a bar of the open spear-topped iron gate at right; a butterfly carved in relief on the slab's front face; clouded night sky with a pale break and distant gothic spires beyond the gate.
reason: Both reviewers are mistaken and the existing description is right. reviewer-a (high confidence) and reviewer-d (medium) independently converged on 'open book', but they converged on the same misreading, and agreement between two reviewers is not evidence when magnification contradicts both. Their two stated pieces of evidence do not survive the zoom: the 'spine gutter V' is in fact a ragged, variable-width tear whose halves are flat and coplanar rather than tented, and the 'wedge of stacked page edges' at the front is the sheet's own torn corner draping over the slab's chamfered edge, a single thin lip with no page block behind it. The decisive detail neither reviewer accounted for is that the split passes straight through the sheet's near edge and divides it into two separately hanging corners; a bound book cannot be open that way. There is also no cover, no boards, no leaves and no binding anywhere on the object. So keyObjects 'torn paper or parchment sheet split by the blade', the scene phrase 'driving a sword point-down into a torn document on a stone slab', and visualTensions 'the intact sheet of paper against its clean tear' all stand, and I reject both reviewers' patches in full, since every one of their proposed edits descends from the book reading. Minor note, not acted on and not a correction: 'clean tear' in visualTensions is a slightly generous description of what is actually a ragged tear, but that is wording, not an observable-fact error, and neither reviewer raised it.
